summary: Chris Williams specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bristol under doctoral supervisor Rita Langer, attested in 2026 as an MPhil and PhD student and teaching staff member.

Christian August Brandis (1790–1867) was a scholar of philosophy and history/archaeology. After studying at Kiel University (~1808–1812), he held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~1812–1815), Humboldt University of Berlin (~1816–1821), and the University of Bonn (~1821–1867).

Christian Bartholomae (1855–1925) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied under Heinrich Hübschmann (~1877–1879) and held posts at Halle-Wittenberg (~1879–1888), Münster (~1889–1898), Giessen (~1898–1901), and Heidelberg University (~1909–1924).

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, where he earned his Magister under supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes and teachers Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Charles Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar of linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied under Christian Gottlob Heyne and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, founded the German Archaeological Institute (1829), and served as Prussian envoy (~1841–1854).

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from the University of Bucharest and the Australian National University under Jay L. Garfield and John Powers. He joined the College of Charleston (~2006) and visited UC Berkeley (2017).

Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a German scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After earning his master's degree at the University of Leipzig (1748–1752), he served as professor at the University of Göttingen (1763) and director of its library (1764–1812).

Christian Haskett specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Witzel, and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer (born 1969) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed his MA and PhD at Columbia University under Robert A. F. Thurman, later teaching at Copenhagen (2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (2003–2011).

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was an Indologist and linguist. After studying at Oslo, Heidelberg, and the University of Bonn under August Wilhelm von Schlegel, he served at Bonn as Privatdozent (1830) and professor of Old Indian language and literature (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke (born 1969) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard University, and Columbia University (PhD ~1997–2003). He served as a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (2003–2007) before joining the University of Washington in 2007.
Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his Magister (1994) and PhD (1998) at the University of Vienna, and has held posts at the University of Vienna (1995) and the Rubin Museum of Art (2012).
Christian Matthias Boehm is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at SOAS University of London, where he completed a PhD attested in 2005, and was taught by Toshifumi Konno.

Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and computational fields. He studied under Seizan Yanagida and held academic posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993, 2008) and Hanazono University (attested 2011).

Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck (1866–1951) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1885–1888). He served as an assistant professor at the University of Amsterdam (1892–1899) and as a professor at Leiden University (1899–1926).

Christine Chojnacki specializes in Indology and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991 and served as a professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Kristofer Schipper and Michel Soymié, and held research posts at the CNRS from 1989 to 1995 and as Director of Research, attested in 2014.

Christmas Humphreys (1901–1983) was an English figure in Buddhist and religious studies. After studying at Malvern College and Trinity Hall, Cambridge (~1919–1922), he served as President of the Buddhist Society from ~1924 to 1983.

Christof Zotter works in Indology and religious studies. In 2018, he is attested as head of the editorial program and postdoctoral researcher at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and as an editorial board member for Documenta Nepalica.
